Seven other metabolites were identified none of which was derived from single-step biotransformation of nitralin. StringWithMarkup.String: Nitralin's former production and use as a selective pre-emergence herbicide may have resulted in its release to the environment. If released to the atmosphere, nitralin will exist primarily in the particulate phase because of its low vapor pressure. It will degrade in the vapor-phase by reaction with photochemically produced hydroxyl radicals with an estimated half-life of 0.64 days. Particulate phase nitralin may be physically removed from the atmosphere via wet and dry deposition. If released to soil, nitralin is expected to have medium to low mobility based on an estimated Koc value of 980. Nitralin is not expected to photodegrade or volatilize from moist or dry soil surfaces. If released to water, nitralin is not expected to volatilize based on an estimated Henry's Law constant of 7X10-9 atm-cu m/mol. However, it may bioconcentrate in aquatic organisms and adsorb to sediment or particulate matter in the water column based on an estimated BCF value of 820 and an estimated Koc value of 980. Biodegradation of nitralin is expected in both aerobic and anaerobic conditions with half-lives of 2.4 to 3.7 months in soil. (SRC)

Section.Description: Sorption to soils and sediments is an important factor on the transport and fate of organic contaminants in the environment.  The soil/water adsorption coefficient, also known as solid-water distribution coefficient (Kd), measures the amount of chemical substance adsorbed onto soil per amount of water.  Since adsorption occurs predominantly by partition into the soil organic matter, it is more useful to normalize the Kd value to the organic carbon content of a soil and express the distribution coefficient in Koc (organic carbon normalized distribution coefficient).  The greater the Kd (or Koc) value, the less likely a chemical will leach or contribute to runoff.  A very high value means it is strongly adsorbed onto soil and organic matter and does not move throughout the soil.
